case: Stephen Elop's February 2011 "burning platform" memo declared Symbian non-competitive days before Nokia announced a Windows Phone pivot; Symbian's share fell by nearly half within two quarters and Elop later conceded to shareholders that the memo hurt Symbian sales.
trigger: Customer-facing copy, changelog, docs, or a public roadmap describes a currently shipping product, framing, or API as deprecated, weak, or superseded before its replacement is available.

name: Sunk Identity
mechanism: A decision defended by prior investment or by "this is what we are" cannot be evaluated, because both premises are facts about the past rather than about the option. The incumbent option gets an unearned advantage precisely in proportion to how much was spent establishing it.
case: In 1985, with memory losing to Japanese competitors, Grove asked Moore what a new CEO brought in by the board would do; Moore said get out of memories. Grove's move was to walk out, walk back in, and do it themselves — Intel exited DRAM, the business that had defined the company.
trigger: A decision or spec is defended by how much has already been built, how long it took, or by identity language ("we're a X company", "this is our thesis"), rather than by the option's forward value.

name: Exit Reason Assumed
mechanism: Churn explanations default to the most legible variable — price, salary, performance — because it is the one already instrumented. The actual reasons are relational and only obtainable by asking, so the retention fix targets the wrong lever and produces no change, which is then read as the problem being intractable.
case: Michael Abrashoff interviewed every sailor on the USS Benfold and found the top reasons for leaving the Navy were not being treated with respect, being prevented from having an impact, and not being listened to. Pay — the reason he had assumed was first — ranked fifth.
trigger: An explanation of attrition, churn, drop-off, or non-adoption asserts a cause (price, speed, missing feature) without citing anything the departed users or teammates actually said.

name: Adding People To A Late Thing
mechanism: New people on a late project consume the time of the people who know the system, and communication paths grow quadratically with headcount, so the near-term effect on a component with tight internal coupling is negative. Partitionable work is the exception, and the work that is late is rarely the partitionable kind.
case: Fred Brooks managed IBM's OS/360 and drew the law from it: adding manpower to a late software project makes it later. OS/360 shipped years late, over budget, and with thousands of known defects despite a headcount peak in the thousands.
trigger: A slipping deliverable is answered by assigning more engineers, more parallel agents, or more concurrent sessions to the same component or file set, rather than by cutting scope.

name: The Famous Forecaster
mechanism: Confidence and reputation are produced by a different process than accuracy, and in public settings they are rewarded more, so the loudest forecast is systematically the least hedged. Without a resolution date and a scoring rule, no forecast ever gets marked wrong, and the calibration signal never reaches anyone.
case: Tetlock's 20-year study collected roughly 28,000 predictions from 284 experts and found they barely beat chance and lost to simple extrapolation rules — with the better-known and more media-visible experts scoring worse, not better.
trigger: A claim about the future (adoption, competitor behavior, market timing, "users will want X") is backed by seniority, conviction, or a cited authority rather than by a dated, falsifiable statement someone will check.

name: One-Way Door, Casual
mechanism: Decisions get processed at the weight of their immediate cost, not their reversibility, so a cheap-to-decline strategic option receives less scrutiny than an expensive-to-build feature. The irreversibility only becomes visible after the window that would have let you act on it has closed.
case: In 2000 Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph offered to sell Netflix to Blockbuster for $50M; Blockbuster declined in a meeting Randolph describes as barely suppressing laughter. Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in 2010.
trigger: A decision that forecloses a future option (a partnership declined, a public API committed, a naming/positioning lock, a data model that cannot be migrated) is being made in the same pass as routine work, with no note distinguishing it.

name: Wartime Frame In Peacetime
mechanism: Consensus-building, broad exploration, and process are correct when the constraint is opportunity and wrong when the constraint is survival — and vice versa. Teams keep whichever mode they last succeeded in, so the mismatch persists exactly through the period where it is most expensive.
case: With Loudcloud's stock near $0.35, Ben Horowitz sold the entire revenue-producing managed-services business to EDS for $63.5M in 2002 and bet the company on unproven software as Opsware — a single narrowed decision made against the diversified one. HP bought Opsware for $1.6B in 2007.
trigger: An existential condition is stated (runway, a competitor shipping the core feature, a broken primary flow, zero users) and the proposed response is a broad multi-track plan, a process change, or a round of alignment.

name: Cofounder Equity Without Vesting
mechanism: Equity granted without vesting or a cliff prices a contribution before it has happened, and the grant survives the contributor's departure, disagreement, or non-performance. The dispute surfaces at the financing or acquisition that makes the equity worth litigating, which is the worst possible moment to have it.
case: Reggie Brown, credited with the disappearing-photo idea, was pushed out of Snapchat early; his suit against Evan Spiegel and Bobby Murphy settled in 2014 for $157.5M, disclosed days before Snap's IPO filing years later.
trigger: A cofounder split, advisor grant, contractor equity arrangement, or early-employee offer is described with a percentage but no vesting schedule, cliff, or repurchase right.

name: The Concealed Constraint
mechanism: When a commercial promise becomes a design constraint that cannot be openly named, the system gets shaped to hide the thing that would violate it rather than to satisfy the underlying requirement. Everyone downstream then reasons about a system whose most load-bearing behavior is undocumented.
case: Boeing owed Southwest a reported $1M-per-plane rebate if the 737 MAX required simulator training; MCAS references were removed from pilot operating and training manuals, and pilots on the Lion Air and Ethiopian flights faced a system they had not been told existed.
trigger: A design or documentation decision is justified by preserving a commercial or compatibility commitment ("no retraining", "no migration", "no API break", "don't scare the customer") rather than by the requirement itself — especially when it removes a mechanism from docs while keeping it in code.
